title: Give People More Time Than They Ask For
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Admired Leadership Field Note argues that showing people they are personally important is one of the most critical tasks in leadership and relationship building. Good leaders go beyond saying so: they respond quickly, anticipate needs, remember details of people's lives and take seriously what matters to them. The piece contends that time carries the most symbolic weight, so leaders who make others feel important give more time than requested, invite more questions when asked one, and extend an invitation to explore the problem more deeply when asked for advice. Because time is the one resource every leader is short on, giving it tells a person where they rank. When people see that they count, they give more of themselves to the relationship, and they never forget who showed them.
points: Leaders show people they matter through responsiveness, anticipation, availability and attention to what is significant to them.
Time spent with and on someone carries the most symbolic weight of all the signals a leader sends.
Responding to a request for a brief conversation with more time than requested is the upgrade that delivers the message.
Because every leader is short on time, giving it tells people where they rank among competing demands.
People who feel they count give more of themselves to the relationship and remember who made them feel that way.
quotes: They remember the details of their lives, show interest in their ideas, and facilitate their goals and passions.
But it is time spent with them and on them that carries the most symbolic weight.
When asked a question, they invite more questions. When asked for a brief conversation, they give more time than requested.
Time is the one resource every leader is short on, and everyone knows it. That’s why giving it speaks so loudly and clearly.
When a leader gives someone more time than they asked for, it tells that person where they rank.
Making room in a busy day or calendar for another person isn’t just being generous. It underlines that the other person matters
When people see they count, they give more of themselves to the relationship. And they never forget who showed them.
